races.name: Prestige Safety Your Trusted Safety Partner Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Further Measure
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with a Southwell 1m6f win on standard going in recent form and a sim-going record of 4 wins from 5 similar-surface runs; prominent racer who should sit comfortably just off Desert Belle and has the course-distance profile to be dangerous.|

runners_data.name: Glenna
runners_data.note: Tom Ward's three-year-old steps up to 1m6f for the first time and has placed at Listed level, but her sim-going record on standard AW surfaces is a concern — 0 wins and 0 places from 2 such runs — and she is untested at this trip.|

runners_data.name: Easwrith Destiny
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's lightly raced three-year-old holds up off the pace by nature and arrives 48 days fresh with only three runs on the board; the step to 1m6f is unexplored territory but her soft-ground form suggests stamina, and she is one to respect at a price.|

runners_data.name: Desert Belle
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's precision operator is the lone front-runner here and has five consecutive Southwell starts with a win and four placings on standard going — the uncontested lead on a flat, galloping track is tailor-made for her.|

runners_data.name: Flash Kozo
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's three-year-old has a course placing over 1m3f on standard but holds up toward the rear; inconsistent form figures including a 16th suggest he is vulnerable, though his best Southwell effort hints at residual course aptitude.|

runners_data.name: Tenison
runners_data.note: Peter Chapple-Hyam's three-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by nature — his Southwell win came from the back — but the crowded rear of this field means he will likely find himself in midfield rather than his preferred position, and his tendency to fade in the closing stages is a further caution.|

runners_data.name: Wave Power
runners_data.note: A true closer who has been pushed into midfield on the map because the back of the field is full; with just one place from five runs on AW-type surfaces and no win, his chances hinge on getting a position and a gap he is unlikely to receive in this shape.|

runners_data.name: Victors Spirit
runners_data.note: Charles Bishop partners this five-year-old who has a solid sim-going record of 1 win and 3 places from 7 standard-surface runs; a hold-up horse who stays well, but needs the pace to be strong and sustained to get into the race from off the bridle.|

runners_data.name: Marbuzet
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby sends out this seven-year-old who has course-distance form at Goodwood over 1m6f and 2m, including two wins at 2m; prominent style suits him tracking Desert Belle, though his most recent runs show a sharp drop in form.|

runners_data.name: It's Only Fun
runners_data.note: Sara Ender's four-year-old is naturally a hold-up horse — her best runs have come from off the pace — but with multiple closers in this field she is pushed toward midfield on the map, making it harder for her to reproduce the held-up style that delivered her Southwell win over 1m3f.|

races.paceDynamic: Desert Belle is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Luke Morris can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this 1m6f Southwell trip — exactly the kind of uncontested lead that suits Sir Mark Prescott's patient, precision operation. Further Measure and Glenna are the two prominent types most likely to track close behind, giving the race a compact early order with the pace neither slow enough to collapse into a sprint finish nor fast enough to burn off held-up horses. The field contains more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Tenison, It's Only Fun and Wave Power are genuine closers but are shown in midfield because the true back of the field is crowded; none of them can be confident of finding clear air at will. A sustainable, single-file gallop on a flat, standard AW surface heavily favours the prominent and front-running profile — those who can dictate or sit just off the pace will control the race throughout and are best placed to resist late challenges.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Desert Belle Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Desert Belle is allowed to stride into an uncontested lead and sets a measured, metronomic gallop that grinds out the hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: Morris settles Desert Belle in front with no rival willing or able to go with him, and Prescott's well-drilled filly converts routine front-running dominance into a winning margin that closes steadily. The prominent runners Further Measure and Glenna are the closest threats but must work to close ground they may never fully recover.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Further Measure or Glenna track Desert Belle closely enough to collar her entering the straight and the pace proves just slow enough to invite a challenge.
scenarios.body: A pedestrian early gallop means the gap between leader and prominent trackers stays minimal, and Further Measure's course-distance form — including a Southwell win over 1m6f — gives him a genuine edge in this shape. Glenna's step up in trip and Tom Ward's strong recent yard form make her the other live threat if she settles cleanly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Finish Through
scenarios.trigger: If Desert Belle sets a genuinely strong pace that drains her rivals' stamina reserves and leaves the race open for closers to pick up late.
scenarios.body: This is the scenario most dependent on horses out of their natural position — Tenison, Wave Power and It's Only Fun are all true hold-up types mapped to midfield, and only if the pace is punishing and the field strings out will they get the gaps they need. Victors Spirit, with course-winning form over similar distances, is better-placed than the redistributed trio to benefit from a strong gallop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Surge, Messy Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace fractures mid-race, jostling occurs for position among the crowded midfield group, and no single horse dominates.
scenarios.body: A chaotic shape with multiple hold-up horses forced forward of their natural position creates interference risk and opens the race to the horse who finds the cleanest passage late. Easwrith Destiny, lightly raced and likely to improve sharply for this extra distance, is the wildcard most likely to benefit from a messy, unstructured race.

watchPoints.text: Desert Belle — if Luke Morris is allowed to dictate from the front without any pressure, Prescott's meticulous preparation and five consecutive Southwell runs could make this a procession; watch for any horse that tries to go with her early, as none appears likely to.|

Further Measure — a nine-year-old in the form of his life with course-distance course-surface credentials; if he gets a good pitch behind Desert Belle and the pace is honest, his finish could be sharp enough to reel her in.|

Tenison and Wave Power — both are genuine closers forced out of their natural position by a congested back of the field; if they are shuffled wider mid-race trying to make progress they could cause interference to Victors Spirit and Easwrith Destiny.|

Glenna — Sean Levey takes over on a three-year-old stepping up markedly in trip for the first time; her dam's stamina profile may mean she stays, but her AW going record suggests the surface is a question mark worth monitoring in the early strides.|

Marbuzet — Tim Easterby's 14-day strike rate of 8 from 86 is poor, and the horse's recent form has dropped sharply from his 2m Goodwood peak; the drop back to 1m6f and AW surface after a run of soft-ground miles is worth flagging as a potential fitness or suitability concern.|

races.name: Prestige Safety First Aid Training Novice Stakes (gbb/gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Turret
runners_data.note: Won last time out over 9f on Soft and holds a course-sim win; natural front-runner who will bowl along from the front uncontested here, though racing over 1m4f for the first time is a query and the STYLE_FIT tag suggests a style not ideally suited should pace pressure materialise.|

runners_data.name: Crack of Thunder
runners_data.note: Trainer Jack Jones has a poor 14-day strike rate (0/15) and this horse has finished 8th, 11th, and 12th in recent starts, fading in finishes; a genuine hold-up type who is pushed into a midfield slot on the map but faces a tough ask in a congested field, and the fade-in-finish flag is damning.|

runners_data.name: Argenteus
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's 3yo has run just once, finishing 7th over 12f on Good ground; its true running style is hold-up yet the field's depth forces it to race off its preferred position, and with only one run to assess and no Standard-going exposure, there is significant uncertainty.|

runners_data.name: Centrum
runners_data.note: John and Thady Gosden 3yo with a headgear flag (p) who finished 8th on Soft last time; this horse is a hold-up type by nature yet the map forces it forward into a midfield position, and the fade-in-finish tag alongside soft-ground form that didn't transfer suggests conditions here may not unlock improvement.|

runners_data.name: Eshowe
runners_data.note: Edward Smyth-Osbourne's 3yo returns from a 231-day absence, having run 12th over 8f on Standard at Southwell; the layoff is substantial, the form run was dire, and the headgear flag (h) combined with the hold-up style pushed into midfield makes this one to treat with extreme caution on comeback.|

runners_data.name: Humphrey
runners_data.note: Lightly raced Gosden 3yo who ran 2nd over 10f on Good; the unknown style flag means tactics are fluid, but Robert Havlin's booking for this powerful yard on a step up in trip is a positive angle, and unexposed horses from this stable can improve sharply.|

runners_data.name: Kokbastau
runners_data.note: Roger Varian 3yo who was 3rd over 10f on Good last time, an encouraging step forward from a 6th on Soft; a genuine hold-up runner who will need traffic to clear, and the form line over 10f suggests the step to 1m4f should not inconvenience him.|

runners_data.name: Sandpyper
runners_data.note: Ran 10th over 11f at Southwell on Standard going last time and carries a fade-in-finish warning; Kevin and Lauren Frost operate at a modest level and this horse's only comparable course-and-going run produced a double-figure finish, making it hard to warm to.|

runners_data.name: Hello Friend
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's lightly raced 3yo has placed twice over 12f including on Standard going at Southwell, giving him genuine sim-going form at this course; Sam James takes the ride and the style is unknown, meaning the horse could slot in anywhere tactically, which is a mild positive.|

runners_data.name: Marianita
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's 3yo faded to 11th at Southwell on Standard last time after a 4th on Good; the fade-in-finish tag is a concern on this track, and despite Hector Crouch's booking, two runs that ended in retreat suggest the Standard Fibresand surface does not play to her strengths.|

runners_data.name: Alfred Wincham
runners_data.note: Claimer Julian Pietropaolo claims 7lbs and this Patrick Neville 4yo has won twice over 12f and 18f on Good ground, showing solid stamina; a genuine prominent runner who naturally slots into the stalking role, and the wins over classic distances suggest the 1m4f trip is right in his wheelhouse.|

runners_data.name: Sharp Move
runners_data.note: William Haggas 4yo returning from 249 days off with a previous Standard-going win at Southwell over 10f; Tom Marquand's booking for a patient handler who wins with fresh horses is notable, and a prominent style means he can track Turret without burning reserves, though the long absence demands respect.|

runners_data.name: Bankatary
runners_data.note: James Owen's 4yo (trainer 14/38 in 14 days, the best strike rate in the race) has won over 16f on Good and finished 4th over 10f; a prominent runner who shapes as a thorough stayer and his trainer's current form is the key angle here — Luke Morris rides.|

runners_data.name: Pic N Mix
runners_data.note: Nick Littmoden's 5yo has run 6th, 6th, 7th, 8th across four runs over 16f, all on Good or Soft; the step down to 1m4f on Standard ground is a notable switch and there is no evidence the horse performs at this trip or on this surface, making it very hard to include.|

races.paceDynamic: Turret is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this 1m4f Southwell AW trip on Standard ground. Alfred Wincham, Sharp Move, and Bankatary are the other prominent-style horses and will push forward to sit just behind Turret, likely forming a small group at the head of affairs without truly pressuring the pace-setter. The large field of 14 contains a heavy concentration of hold-up horses — Crack of Thunder, Argenteus, Centrum, Eshowe, Sandpyper, Marianita, Kokbastau, and Pic N Mix are all true rear-runners who cannot all secure their natural position and will be shuffled into a congested midfield pack, with only those who navigate traffic cleanly holding any realistic chance of finishing through. This race shape — a lone front-runner allowed to bowl along at a measured clip — strongly favours runners that can sit prominent or just behind the lead and sustain their effort through the home straight, rather than closers who must weave through traffic from a genuine hold-up position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Turret Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Turret sets an uncontested, measured pace and the prominent horses behind track smoothly into the straight.
scenarios.body: Turret dictates the tempo alone, allowing Alfred Wincham, Sharp Move, and Bankatary to sit in a perfect stalking position without burning energy; the horse with the most class and freshness among these prominent types strikes turning in and resists the closers who face traffic. This shape is the dominant probability because the pace map is clear-cut and riders on prominent horses have first use of the rail and clean daylight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Traffic Nightmare, One Closer Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the midfield pack is so congested that one hold-up horse finds a gap late and swoops past tired leaders.
scenarios.body: The slow-burn pace set by Turret paradoxically compresses the field into a tight bunch turning for home, and if a hold-up horse like Kokbastau or Hello Friend finds clear running at the right moment they can pick off a fading leader. This scenario is discounted because the majority of closers carry redistribution tags and face genuine positional disadvantage in a field this size.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Turret Outstayed
scenarios.trigger: If Alfred Wincham or Bankatary push forward to challenge Turret early in the straight and force a genuine test of stamina.
scenarios.body: A contested front end would string the field out and expose any hold-up horses even further, but could also find out Turret if it has set too fast a gallop trying to repel pressure; an unexposed type like Humphrey or Alfred Wincham with proven stamina could benefit from the strongly-run test. The probability is limited because no rider has an obvious incentive to force the pace given the tactical setup.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddling Pace, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so modest that the entire field travels in a compressed group and the race becomes a sprint from 2f out.
scenarios.body: An ultra-slow gallop would theoretically bring the hold-up horses back into contention, but with so many true closers unable to secure their natural position and likely getting bumped in a sprint finish, the advantage still rests with horses handily placed; this is the least likely shape given Turret's natural inclination to bowl along at a fair clip. Sandpyper and Marianita are too far back and fade-prone to capitalise on the confusion.

watchPoints.text: Bankatary's trainer James Owen is among the sharpest operators in the data at 14-day strike rate (14/38) — watch for this prominent stayer to be ridden aggressively into a prime position behind Turret and deliver a sustained challenge in the straight.

Alfred Wincham drops significantly in class with a 7lb claimer but has won twice over staying distances on Good; if the inexperienced jockey executes a clean prominent ride, this horse's stamina profile could prove superior to rivals by the final furlong.

Sharp Move's 249-day absence is the longest layoff in the field — watch for signs of ring-rustiness in the early exchanges despite Haggas horses often running well fresh, particularly as Standard Southwell AW can expose a horse that isn't fully tuned.

The congested midfield pack of six-plus hold-up types creates a traffic flashpoint turning into the straight — watch for interference between Kokbastau, Crack of Thunder, and Hello Friend as riders angle for a gap simultaneously, which could compromise multiple closers at once.

Turret's front-running role is confirmed but this is its first start over 1m4f and it has only run twice; if it sets a pace that is too slow, watch for Alfred Wincham or Bankatary to push alongside and turn this into a stamina test from the 3f pole.

races.name: Prestige Safety E-learning @ Prestigesafetyservices.com Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Avenger
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist with only 2 places from 6 runs on similar going; steps up to 1m3f for the first time and was beaten at long odds-on last time — needs everything to fall right from the rear.|

runners_data.name: Roc De Fer
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott runner on a steady upward trajectory with 3 runs at Southwell, but a true hold-up horse whose deep closing style will see it squeezed out in a rear-heavy field — won't get the clear passage it needs.|

runners_data.name: Five Moons
runners_data.note: Simon & Ed Crisford three-year-old who has finished 4th in five consecutive starts — consistent but seemingly limited, and its genuine hold-up style means it will be buried in the back half of a crowded field.|

runners_data.name: Sun Lord
runners_data.note: Style unknown from just three runs; has a soft-ground win over 11f suggesting stamina, but this is its first try on an AW surface and the form lack makes this a speculative inclusion.|

runners_data.name: Alkumatic Jo Jo
runners_data.note: The race-shaper — lone confirmed front-runner under De Sousa, uncontested in front and able to dictate at will; has two places from five at Southwell though yet to win, and the step up to 1m3f is a question mark.|

runners_data.name: Miss Pretty
runners_data.note: Only genuine prominent runner in the field behind the pace-setter, with a Southwell win to her name and a solid place record here; first-time headgear noted, and her ability to sit second or third is a major positional advantage.|

runners_data.name: Brave Leader
runners_data.note: Tom Ward runner whose four-runner place record includes two placings on AW, but its true hold-up profile means it will be doing its best work behind a wall of horses turning for home; first-time headgear applied.|

runners_data.name: Carwyn
runners_data.note: Tagged as a horse that fades in the finish — a damaging trait in a race where closers already face a traffic problem; nine consecutive defeats and no visible angle make this very hard to recommend.|

runners_data.name: Tinsel
runners_data.note: PJ McDonald takes over on a horse that won over 10f at Southwell and has three runs on the surface — best course form in this field among the hold-up horses; the 83-day break is the key concern, but Hughie Morrison horses often return fit.|

runners_data.name: Seraglio Point
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand rides for Hughie Morrison, giving the yard a double entry with Tinsel; only three career runs and just one piece of Southwell form — inexperienced and hard to assess, but stable angle worth noting.|

runners_data.name: Prince Of Calypso
runners_data.note: Highest-rated horse in the field at OR 70 alongside Corallience, but three runs show only a place on soft ground; first-time headgear on, and Billy Loughnane rides — its genuine hold-up style will see it tracking a crowded rear pack.|

runners_data.name: Corallience
runners_data.note: David Menuisier runner at OR 70 with modest form — a sixth on Southwell fibresand and two worse efforts; hold-up style in a field where that position is oversubscribed, and 53 days off adds to the question marks.|

runners_data.name: James Choice
runners_data.note: Unknown running style giving Warren Greatrex flexibility to place this one forward if wanted; one place from four similar-going runs and a jockey/trainer combination with limited recent form — one to assess in running.|

runners_data.name: Fans Favourite
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's three-year-old arrives in career-best form with back-to-back wins on soft ground, but has no AW fibresand form and the surface switch is a genuine concern; hold-up style means it faces the same positional challenges as the rest of the rear group.|

races.paceDynamic: Alkumatic Jo Jo is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner field and, with Silvestre De Sousa aboard, will stride to the front from the outset and control tempo over this 1m3f Southwell fibresand trip at a sustainable, uncontested pace. The field is loaded with hold-up horses — Roc De Fer, Five Moons, Brave Leader, Carwyn, Tinsel, Prince Of Calypso, Corallience, Fans Favourite and Ziggy's Avenger all carry hold-up profiles — meaning the rear of the race will be crowded and many will be unable to secure their preferred position. Miss Pretty and, to a lesser extent, Sun Lord and James Choice (both style-unknown) represent the most likely horses to travel prominently in behind Alkumatic Jo Jo, with Miss Pretty — the only genuine prominent type — best placed to sit second or third. With one horse controlling an uncontested, measured pace from the front, the race shape strongly favours prominent runners and those able to travel close to the action, as closers from deep in the pack will need to navigate traffic and generate momentum from a standing start in a compressed finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Alkumatic Jo Jo Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Alkumatic Jo Jo leads at a comfortable tempo and no rival has the will or ability to close the gap from the home bend.
scenarios.body: De Sousa controls every yard from the front, setting a honest but not suicidal pace that bleeds the closers dry on the run-in; the moderate gallop suits horses travelling close to the pace who can quicken off a relatively even tempo.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If a horse travelling just off the pace — Miss Pretty or an unknown-style runner — produces a clean burst around the home turn to swamp Alkumatic Jo Jo.
scenarios.body: The steady front-running pace sets up a sharp finishing burst from the horse positioned second or third, and Miss Pretty's prior win at Southwell and her prominent style make her the prime beneficiary; Sun Lord or James Choice, if they elect to race positively, could also land this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Storm Through
scenarios.trigger: If the tempo is faster than expected and the field fans wide in the straight, creating clear ground for the rear-of-field horses.
scenarios.body: A faster early pace would compress the field into a wall turning in, but horses with the best form on the surface — Tinsel (winner over course and distance) and Fans Favourite (back-to-back wins, in-form) — could thread through; this scenario is discounted because the field is packed with genuine hold-up types who will crowd the finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Hold-Ups Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If Alkumatic Jo Jo fades sharply in the final two furlongs after front-running alone, gifting the hold-up horses a clear run.
scenarios.body: A complete implosion of the pace-setter is required, and even then the mass of hold-up horses will compete with one another for the same ground; this scenario is the least likely given the field's redistributed nature means few true closers will get clean air.

watchPoints.text: Alkumatic Jo Jo — if De Sousa winds the pace up even marginally, watch whether Miss Pretty can stay in contact; if the gap grows by halfway, the prominent scenario collapses entirely.
Miss Pretty — first-time headgear on a horse that has mixed form including a win at Southwell; if she races keenly or too close to a dawdling pace-setter she could burn out before the straight.
Tinsel — the 83-day layoff for Hughie Morrison's course winner is the critical watch; if she shows any signs of ring-rustiness in the first two furlongs, discount her late-run scenario significantly.

Rear-group traffic — with six or more genuine hold-up horses competing for the same ground on the inside rail at Southwell's tight circuit, any runner drawn into the middle of the pack without early daylight faces a severe traffic problem turning in.

Fans Favourite — back-to-back wins on soft ground create a profile that looks strong on paper, but no fibresand experience whatsoever means the surface response in the early furlongs is the key piece of information to gather.

races.name: Prestige Safety Fire Risk Assessments Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Thisonesforyou
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Good going but Southwell Fibresand is a new test; Clive Cox runner ridden by Georgia Dobie, and while the pace role suits the race shape, the STYLE_FIT flag suggests she may not hold this front position with full conviction — treat the lead as functional rather than dominant.

runners_data.name: Kiani King
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane's booking is significant for Hughie Morrison but this horse is a genuine hold-up type with only three starts; 67 days off and no Fibresand form means plenty of unknowns, and he'll be sitting well off the pace in a race where late ground is at a premium.

runners_data.name: Mehmas Engine
runners_data.note: Rhys Clutterbuck takes the ride for Luke Dace; a known fader in the finish based on race history, and the redistribution to midfield on the map understates how far back this horse will genuinely be — combined with a string of nines in recent form, hard to be confident.

runners_data.name: Bosom Pals
runners_data.note: Won on Good going over 7f for Tom Dascombe but has been well beaten in several subsequent efforts; William Cox rides, and as a true rear-of-field runner who will be competing for the same late ground as multiple similar types, the cluttered closing section is a real threat to a clean run.

runners_data.name: Back At One
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's three-run juvenile has only raced on Standard and Soft and finished no better than fifth; Ray Dawson rides, and while the stable has a decent 14-day strike rate, this horse is a hold-up type with limited evidence it can overhaul rivals from off the pace here.

runners_data.name: Topathemorning
runners_data.note: Jack Doughty partners Stuart Williams's runner who has shown ability over this trip on Standard going; a hold-up horse by nature, sitting at the rear, but the form figure of 5 at Southwell over 8f is the most relevant piece in the book and he deserves respect if he gets a clear run.

runners_data.name: Sagremor
runners_data.note: David Menuisier sends Sean Levey north for this; a hold-up horse whose best Southwell form is a third but has also been beaten well on the surface — headgear worn, 66 days off, and will need a stronger pace than Thisonesforyou is likely to set to make ground effectively.

runners_data.name: Venetian Lion
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand for William Haggas is an eye-catching booking at the top level; headgear worn, three runs all on Standard going and best finish a sixth, but the yard's quality and Marquand's ability to find gaps from hold-up positions makes this one of the more interesting closers in the field.

runners_data.name: Filly Eilish
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa on for Ivan Furtado; ran second over 10f on Standard and placed in both Southwell runs over this trip, suggesting a genuine affinity with the track and distance — a hold-up horse by style but with a notable course angle that elevates her above many rivals in this section.

runners_data.name: Cobalt Comet
runners_data.note: P J McDonald takes the ride for John Mackie; won last time on Good and has hit the frame multiple times on Standard going, including at this course — a prominent racer who should sit close to Thisonesforyou and is ideally positioned in this race shape, with the headgear flag indicating an active yard.

runners_data.name: Telfy Boy
runners_data.note: Luke Morris rides for Martin Dunne; 277 days off the track is a significant concern and the unknown running style (U) makes pace mapping difficult — Southwell form includes a second over 8f on Standard which is relevant, but such a long layoff demands caution regardless.

runners_data.name: Alkaios
runners_data.note: Dougie Costello partners Steph Hollinshead's runner; a hold-up horse that fades in the finish based on race data, has been beaten nine lengths or more in recent outings including twice on Standard, and even being mapped to midfield flatters where this horse is likely to be — very hard to recommend.

runners_data.name: Hatamoto
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's prolific sort ridden by Sean Kirrane; two wins from last three runs all on Good going is a concern for Fibresand Standard, but the prominent racing style puts him in an ideal tactical spot and the form is the best in the race on raw numbers — the going switch is the key variable to resolve.

runners_data.name: Medyg
runners_data.note: Alistair Rawlinson for Edward Smyth-Osbourne; headgear worn and the preferred going is listed as Polytrack (p flag), which may mean Fibresand Standard is acceptable — true hold-up style that the map has shifted to midfield, recent form figures of 8 and 9 make it hard to enthuse despite the course surface angle.

races.paceDynamic: Thisonesforyou is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 14-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should settle into a comfortable, uncontested gallop from the outset on Southwell's flat Fibresand circuit. Cobalt Comet and Hatamoto are the most likely prominent companions, sitting just behind the pace and applying enough pressure to keep the tempo honest without turning it into a war. The bulk of the field — Topathemorning, Sagremor, Venetian Lion, Filly Eilish and several others — are genuine hold-up types who will fan out in the straight and look for gaps from the rear. This shape, with a lone, relaxed leader setting a sustainable gallop, classically favours horses who can travel prominently and kick off a genuine pace — Cobalt Comet and Hatamoto are best placed tactically — though the sheer volume of hold-up horses means a late surge is always possible if the pace is insufficient to string the field out. Note that the field contains far more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear; Kiani King, Mehmas Engine, Bosom Pals, Back At One, Alkaios and Medyg are all genuine closers who will be jostling for the same ground late, reducing the effectiveness of any one of them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Thisonesforyou bowls along unchallenged and sets a fair but controlled gallop, the horses closest to the pace get first run.
scenarios.body: Thisonesforyou dictates every yard of a steady-to-fair tempo with Cobalt Comet and Hatamoto tracking in her slipstream, and when the sprint begins those prominent racers have the best position to pounce; the hold-up brigade face too much traffic negotiating through a tightly bunched field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Cobalt Comet or Hatamoto push the leader hard enough to soften the pace for a sweeping midfield challenge.
scenarios.body: The early gallop becomes honest rather than dawdling, stretching the field and giving the best-travelling midfield horses — particularly those with stronger form — a clear run to the line; Topathemorning and Venetian Lion have the class to benefit from this configuration.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Swamp the Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs and the whole field bunches, creating a chaotic sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A slow or uneven gallop compresses the pack and the finishing straight becomes a cavalry charge; however, many of the nominal closers here are redistributed hold-up types not truly at home making ground late on Fibresand, which blunts this scenario's plausibility considerably.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Hangs On
scenarios.trigger: If Thisonesforyou finds an uncharacteristically strong gallop rhythm and the hold-up field is given too much to do.
scenarios.body: Racing on the front end without serious pressure from Cobalt Comet or Hatamoto, Thisonesforyou could steal enough of a break that the chasing pack simply runs out of track; this outcome is limited in probability by the horse's style-fit concern and the competitive quality of the prominent trackers.

watchPoints.text: Hatamoto's going preference is the pivotal unknown — if Tim Easterby's horse handles Fibresand Standard as well as Good, his prominent style and sharp recent form make him the most dangerous runner in the race.

With Kiani King, Bosom Pals, Back At One, Alkaios and Medyg all seeking the same late ground, watch for severe congestion in the straight — any of these horses drawn wide or caught in traffic could lose several lengths before finding clear air.

Thisonesforyou's STYLE_FIT flag means the front position is less secure than it appears; if Cobalt Comet or Hatamoto push up early, the supposedly controlled pace could become genuinely hot and change the complexion of the race entirely.

Venetian Lion's Tom Marquand booking for William Haggas stands out as an unusual trainer-jockey combination for this grade at Southwell — watch whether the market shortens this horse on the morning of the race as an indicator of stable confidence.

Telfy Boy's 277-day absence is the longest layoff in the field by a significant margin; Luke Morris will likely ride him cold, and any signs of greenness or fitness issues early will confirm this horse can be safely overlooked on the day.

races.name: Prestige Safety Your Competent H&S Service Ebf Restricted Novice Stakes (for Horses In Bands B, C And D) (Ebf Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Prestige Safety Construction Safety Specialists Handicap Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Bloodsweatandtyres
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Brian Ellison with decent sim-going form (1W2P in 4 runs) but the flat, one-bend Southwell layout offers limited late cover and no downhill run to aid a closing burst; 30 days fresh and wears a hood, which can sharpen focus but not compensate for a race likely to lack the truly strong pace this style requires.

runners_data.name: Asteverdi
runners_data.note: Luke Morris takes the ride on this hold-up operator, but all recent form comes over 8-10f on soft or good ground, and a drop to 7f on Fibresand standard may catch him a touch short of his best conditions; 52 days off the track adds an element of doubt.

runners_data.name: Tropez Power
runners_data.note: Jack Garritty partners this seven-year-old hold-up type whose recent form string of 5-6-6-8-8 tells its own story — zero wins or places from 15 runs on sim-going and no obvious reason the pattern reverses here.

runners_data.name: Peter The Wolf
runners_data.note: Edward Greatrex inherits the ride on this hold-up type whose sole win came over 6f on soft ground, and the step up to 7f on a flat AW track does not obviously suit a horse who has finished outside the top six in five of the last six; trainer Warren Greatrex has had no winners from five runners in the last 14 days.

runners_data.name: Storm Free
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner at OR 86 who can set his own terms and dictate the gallop; Hector Crouch is an assured front-riding partner, the sim-going record includes four placed efforts, and an uncontested lead on a flat track is about as good as conditions get — though the STYLE_FIT tag reminds that finishing off a race from the front is not always guaranteed.

runners_data.name: Breakdancer
runners_data.note: Silvestre De Sousa brings top-level handling to Crisford's consistent performer whose form figures at 7-8f show two wins and two places from his last five and five placed efforts in 11 AW runs; races prominently and will be ideally positioned to challenge if Storm Free's gallop is catchable.

runners_data.name: Chalk Mountain
runners_data.note: Two wins at Southwell on standard going make this Alfie Redman (7lb claimer) mount one of the most course-specific entries in the field; the tongue-tie is retained, he races prominently, and his last two runs here both resulted in wins at 7f — the track clearly brings out his best.

runners_data.name: City Of Kings
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen, better known over jumps but capable on the flat, partners this prominent-racing type who has one win at Goodwood but a recent blank (11th, 6th) and a 46-day break; the step back to AW from turf soft ground could help, though his sim-going record is limited.

runners_data.name: Ash Wednesday
runners_data.note: Daniel Muscutt rides a horse whose sim-going record is outstanding (6W8P from 12 runs, 12 of 15 on similar going) — the raw numbers are compelling, but 88 days off the track is a significant flag; a natural prominent-racing type who has been mapped back to midfield given the crowded front end, meaning he may not access his preferred position as freely as usual.

runners_data.name: Spaceman
runners_data.note: Oisin Orr takes this lightly-raced three-year-old who owns a win and a place from two runs on standard AW — promising profile, and the step up from 5-6f to 7f is the main unknown; races prominently and has the raw speed to mix it with the pace-setters if the trip proves within range.

runners_data.name: Lucky Luna
runners_data.note: Sean Levey and Richard Hannon team up with a three-year-old filly whose sole win came on soft ground over 7f — she wants to race up with the pace, but in a field stacked with prominent types she is likely to be shuffled wider and further back than ideal, diluting the advantage that style brings.

runners_data.name: Exotic Baby
runners_data.note: George Boughey's juvenile is a natural hold-up type, but with so many closers already at the rear this filly has been mapped further forward than she will naturally travel; Jack Doughty is a capable conditional, and her 4th in an AW 7f last time out hints at competence at the trip, but racing out of her natural role is a structural disadvantage.

races.paceDynamic: Storm Free is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should be able to dictate from the front at a measured, sustainable gallop over this flat Southwell 7f. Behind him, Breakdancer, Chalk Mountain, City Of Kings, and Spaceman will jostle for the prominent berths, creating a moderately competitive early order but not a true pace duel that would burn Storm Free off. With the pace controlled and relatively honest rather than brutal, horses who can sit just off the tempo and quicken through the final two furlongs are best placed — making the handy, prominent profile the primary beneficiary. The field contains more horses that prefer to race prominently than can physically secure those positions, and Storm Free, Breakdancer, and City Of Kings are most likely to actually hold the prominent slots, with Lucky Luna and Ash Wednesday — both natural front-to-prominent types — liable to find themselves racing further back than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Storm Free Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Storm Free leads without serious pressure and the pace is honest but not frantic, allowing him to quicken away.
scenarios.body: Storm Free sets a metronomic gallop on the flat Southwell track, denying rivals any slow-pace sprint they could exploit, and his high STYLE_FIT score at this level means he is operating within himself until the turn for home; the horses best placed to pounce are those travelling prominently in his slipstream who can match his change of gear.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle Home
scenarios.trigger: If Storm Free is pressed harder than expected by Breakdancer or City Of Kings through the middle portion, lifting the pace and setting up a two-way fight to the line.
scenarios.body: A contested lead through the belly of the race increases early oxygen debt, meaning only those who tracked the speed without burning surplus energy can sustain their effort in the final furlong; Breakdancer's consistency at this trip and Spaceman's sharp early speed give them the engine to capitalise if the principals tire.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough from the front to string the field out and leave a gap for a late-finishing hold-up type.
scenarios.body: Bloodsweatandtyres or Asteverdi would need their natural closing run to materialise off a genuine strong gallop, but the flat Southwell circuit with one true pace-setter makes this a harder scenario to execute than it appears; Exotic Baby, though redistributed from its natural hold-up role, has course form to draw on if the race develops into a proper test.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Irrelevant
scenarios.trigger: If Storm Free's unchallenged lead turns into a dawdle that bunches the field and produces a sprint finish from halfway.
scenarios.body: A slow early tempo compresses the field and strips hold-up horses of their biggest weapon — the ability to pass horses already beaten for toe — and instead rewards those with the sharpest acceleration from a standing sprint; Chalk Mountain's two wins at this course and Spaceman's raw speed make them the natural inheritors of this shape.

watchPoints.text: Storm Free — if Hector Crouch gets a clean break and no rival is willing to pressure him through the first two furlongs, he could effectively run his own race and remain hard to reel in for the prominent horses tracking him.

Breakdancer and City Of Kings — both will want to race in the first two or three from the front, and a battle for position early between them and Storm Free could materially lift the pace and alter the race shape, benefiting hold-up types if it does.

Ash Wednesday — 88 days off the track combined with a crowded prominent section means this horse with outstanding AW sim-going figures (6W from 12) may simply not get the run of the race; watch whether Muscutt can find a line that partially recovers the lost position.

Chalk Mountain — two Southwell wins at this exact trip and going should not be underrated; if Alfie Redman (7lb claim) can slot into a handy berth just behind Storm Free, the course familiarity could prove decisive at a big price.

Spaceman — only three career runs makes this Fahey three-year-old a wildcard; if the step up to 7f suits, the AW sim-going form (1W2P from 3) and Oisin Orr partnership makes him one to monitor from a prominent position through the final quarter-mile.

races.name: Prestige Safety Construction Safety Specialists Handicap Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: King Of Fury
runners_data.note: Course-and-distance winner on Standard Fibresand (1 win from 2 tries sim-going), but that effort is now some runs ago and his recent form figures of 7-6-5-4 suggest a horse who is consistently finding the places just out of reach; hold-up style means he needs others to set the race up, and with a controlled pace that may not happen.

runners_data.name: Shaman Champion
runners_data.note: A 3-year-old from Clive Cox stepping back from Good ground where his last four runs produced no better than eighth; the Southwell switch is the key unknown and Callum Rodriguez takes over, but his recent form figures of 8-10-7 on Good make him hard to trust until he shows Fibresand suits.

runners_data.name: White Crown Star
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' 4-year-old carries solid placed form at this course (two top-3s at 7f/STA) and the trip and ground are demonstrably suitable, but he is a natural front-runner who will find positions already claimed by Eminency — expect him to race in a more restrained role than his profile demands, which is a genuine tactical handicap.

runners_data.name: Star Of Mali
runners_data.note: Excellent course record — four of his last five runs on Standard Fibresand produced a win or place, including back-to-back wins at 7f/STA — but James Tate's 4-year-old is a natural prominent racer who finds the pace map congested; Hector Crouch will need to be patient in a race where his horse wants to be prominent, and any energy spent fighting for position early is energy not spent at the finish.

runners_data.name: Cogitate
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's 5-year-old carries top weight (142lbs) alongside Eminency and brings headgear (p — presumably a hood or similar) which is worth noting; his only sim-going run came in a placed effort at 7f/STA and he is a genuine prominent type who should slot in cleanly behind Eminency without redistribution issues, making him one of the more naturally placed runners.

runners_data.name: Eminency
runners_data.note: The race's confirmed pace-setter, Stuart Williams' 6-year-old carries 142lbs but has placed at this course and distance multiple times on Standard; the [STYLE_FIT] tag reflects that he is being asked to lead, which is his natural role, but the concern is that from a top-weight burden and 51 days off, sustaining that lead across 7f on Fibresand may test his stamina reserves in the final furlong.

runners_data.name: Padua
runners_data.note: Hughie Morrison's 4-year-old has a course win at 7f/GOO but his Fibresand sim-going record (1 placed from 4) is modest; Billy Loughnane takes over and the horse wears a tongue tie — he is a natural prominent racer but with Eminency, Cogitate and Shaman Champion ahead of him in the queue, he will likely find himself racing more patiently than he would prefer, which blunts his effectiveness.

runners_data.name: Comic Hero
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's 3-year-old has a Southwell win at 7f/STA and a placed effort at 6f on Good, giving him genuine Fibresand credentials that stand out in this field; P J McDonald rides and Comic Hero is a proper prominent type who is not affected by redistribution, meaning he should get his natural position tucked in behind Eminency — the strongest profile fit in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Feel The Need
runners_data.note: Michael Herrington's 6-year-old is a true hold-up horse mapped honestly at the rear; his only placed effort on sim-going came at 7f/STA but his last three races on Good produced finishes of 13th, 21st and 16th, and with a single controlled pace-setter, the conditions do not set up for a late swooper — Alistair Rawlinson faces a tough task.

runners_data.name: Chale Chalo
runners_data.note: Tom Dascombe's 3-year-old brings excellent course form — wins and places at 7f/STA — and Tom Marquand is a strong booking; he wears headgear (p) and is a hold-up type who will need the pace to have cut up the front-runners before the straight, which in a single-pace-setter scenario is a genuine concern despite his obvious track affinity.

runners_data.name: Korbut
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's 3-year-old is a model of consistency — five of his last six runs on Standard Fibresand produced a top-2 finish — and Luke Morris retains the ride; he is a genuine hold-up type who knows how to find the line at this track, and his freshness (10 days since last run, Prescott often times horses precisely) makes him the most dangerous closer if anything transpires to quicken the pace mid-race.

races.paceDynamic: Eminency is the confirmed front-runner and will lead from the outset at Southwell's 7f on Standard Fibresand, setting a sustainable and largely uncontested gallop that suits his hold-the-front profile. Behind him, a cluster of genuine prominent racers — White Crown Star, Star Of Mali, Padua, and Shaman Champion — are all jostling for the same early positions, meaning at least two or three will be forced to race further back than their natural inclination, burning energy fighting for berth or settling in unfamiliar midfield slots. Comic Hero and Cogitate are the prominent types best-placed to naturally slot in behind Eminency without excessive early use, while the redistributed horses (White Crown Star, Star Of Mali, Padua) face the reality of racing out of role. With a single controlled pace-setter dictating a fair but not punishing tempo on a flat track, this race shape primarily favours horses who can sit a length or two off the leader and deliver a measured, sustained finish — making the on-pace profile of Comic Hero and Cogitate most naturally aligned, while hold-up horses like Korbut and Chale Chalo will need a pace injection that may not arrive.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Eminency Leads, On-Pace Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Eminency controls from the front at a fair clip and the prominent types immediately behind deliver the finishing effort.
scenarios.body: Eminency dictates a measured gallop and the field strings out on the flat Southwell straight, rewarding horses that have tracked economically in the slipstream; Comic Hero and Cogitate, both genuine prominent types with sim-going form at this track, are positioned to pounce entering the final furlong without having burned reserves in early positional battles. Korbut and Chale Chalo will find themselves too far back to reel in a well-judged leader unless the gallop quickens dramatically.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Stolen Lead
scenarios.trigger: If Eminency is allowed to steal an uncontested lead and the pack fails to close the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: Eminency, ridden by Sean Levey and trained by Stuart Williams who knows this track well, exploits a hesitant response from the chasing pack on Standard ground where front-runners historically hold on; the redistribution squeeze among White Crown Star, Star Of Mali and Padua leaves chasers tangled mid-pack and unable to mount a coordinated challenge. Eminency's form includes placed efforts at this course and distance, giving the bold-front option genuine plausibility if the pace is truly unchallenged.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Charge Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is faster than expected — perhaps Star Of Mali or White Crown Star pressures Eminency — and front-runners tie up in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A genuine pace battle would string the field out and create a weakening leader, opening the door for hold-up horses Korbut and Chale Chalo, both of whom have shown the ability to finish powerfully at this trip on Standard; Korbut's remarkable consistency (five seconds in recent form) suggests he finds the line well when there is something to aim at. King Of Fury, with a win at this course and distance in his profile, also becomes relevant if he can close from the rear.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Implodes, Backmarkers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types clash for position early, setting an unsustainably fast pace that benefits the true hold-up horses sweeping through.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires the redistributed cluster — White Crown Star, Star Of Mali, Padua — to actively fight for front rank and burn out the race, which contradicts the redistribution analysis that places them out of role and less likely to dominate early; even if it materialises, genuine hold-up types in this field such as King Of Fury and Feel The Need have modest sim-going records and limited recent form to suggest they can capitalise efficiently. A low-probability shape precisely because the horses needed to set it up have been mapped away from natural positions.

watchPoints.text: Korbut's Fibresand consistency (0W but five places) and Prescott's precise timing of this runner 10 days off his last run means he could be a dark closer if Eminency's gallop has any pace injection in the final two furlongs.

Star Of Mali's course record (wins at 7f/STA) is the standout sim-going profile in the field — if Hector Crouch manages to get him into a prominent position without burning reserves, his natural affinity for Southwell makes him a real threat to the settled order.

Watch the opening furlong for White Crown Star, Padua and Star Of Mali — all natural prominent types with nowhere to go; if two or three of them push forward aggressively against Eminency, the early pace could be significantly faster than the single front-runner narrative suggests, which would entirely reshape the scenario probabilities.

Comic Hero is 44 days off his last run and drops back from 8f to 7f — his Southwell win came at this trip but connections should be monitored for market moves, as the layoff on a track that rewards freshness could go either way.

Feel The Need's recent form on Good ground (13th, 21st in last two) is starkly different from his one placed effort on Standard — if Standard Fibresand represents a significant surface switch, any market support would be notable given how poorly he has run on other surfaces.

races.name: Prestige Safety Services PPE And Workwear Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Bright
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with a recent Southwell win on Standard (1/6f/STA), jockey Billy Loughnane retains the ride, and the horse has strong similar-going form; will need cover and a fast enough pace to peel off the back, which this moderate gallop may not supply.

runners_data.name: Irish Nectar
runners_data.note: Blinkered hold-up type whose best Standard-going efforts have been placed at 5f-6f; Connor Planas takes over for Herrington, 31 days off track, and with limited Southwell AW wins in the dataset this is an each-way outsider relying on others to force the pace.

runners_data.name: Hierarchy
runners_data.note: Tongue-tied, hold-up operator with the strongest similar-going placed record in the field (3W5P from 12 runs at Standard); William Carver rode well here recently and if the pace is honest enough Hierarchy's ability to close from off the bridle makes it a genuine each-way player.

runners_data.name: D Flawless
runners_data.note: A genuine closer by nature, hooded, with a Southwell Standard win on the card, but forced into a midfield map position in this pace-heavy field — its best chance lies in a scenario where the early tempo is brisk enough for it to make ground from off the pace in the straight.

runners_data.name: Beyond Borders
runners_data.note: Won on Standard at Southwell (1/6f/STA) and carries strong place form on Good, but as a natural hold-up horse nudged into a midfield role by the size of this hold-up contingent, securing a clean run through traffic will be its primary challenge rather than fitness or ability.

runners_data.name: Fifty Nifty
runners_data.note: Equipped with eye-shield, a hold-up type who has been consistent at Southwell in Standard (four runs, 0W0P in sim-going) but is placed midfield only because the back of the field is overcrowded; De Sousa is a significant booking for trainer Martin Dunne but the race shape does not suit.

runners_data.name: Not Me
runners_data.note: Won over 8f on Soft but all recent starts are over shorter, and this is a drop back to 6f on Standard — a natural closer whose best form came on a completely different trip and surface, making this a difficult ask even before factoring in the tactical compromise forced by a crowded hold-up group.

runners_data.name: Modern Times
runners_data.note: Tongue-tied, a hold-up performer with placed efforts on Good but no wins at Standard going; 51 days off track and Luke Morris rides for a prolific James Owen yard, though the absence and style compromise make it hard to see this winning from a midfield position in a controlled-pace race.

runners_data.name: Cairdeas
runners_data.note: Two placed efforts at 6f on Good and a poor run on Standard; David Nolan takes over for Midgley (stable also run D Flawless), 37-day absence, and while the horse has placed form over 6f it has not shown it can win off the pace in this kind of race shape.

runners_data.name: Pickersgill
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Standard for Jardine and has good placed efforts at the trip; Josephine Gordon rides, 10 days between runs, and the drop to 6f is a slight unknown — but the horse's ability to quicken from a mid-rear position gives it an outside chance if the pace collapses.

runners_data.name: Liosa
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner with excellent 6f course form (3W6P at sim-going), Hector Crouch takes over just two days after a previous run which needs monitoring, but the style fits perfectly for a race where tracking the sole front-runner is the premium position.

runners_data.name: Belsito
runners_data.note: Prominent racer fitted with a hood, Kevin Stott rides for Kevin Ryan (0/19 T14 but high-class stable), and a 53-day absence is a minor query; however, the horse's most recent win was at 6f on Standard (1/6f/STA) and its style positions it ideally in this pace scenario.

runners_data.name: Secret Guest
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Bryan Smart, 44 days off, and a barren run of form (058650) with no wins on Standard or Good in recent starts; Ben Robinson rides but there is little in the profile to suggest this shape or track surface will unlock improvement.

runners_data.name: Monsieur Kodi
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner, Oisin Orr in the plate for the Fahey yard; has form at 6f-7f on Standard and this is its natural role, though the STYLE_FIT tag reflects that on a flat course with a large field it must dictate without overdoing the pace — its chance depends on the tempo it sets being sustainable.

races.paceDynamic: Monsieur Kodi is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner 6f handicap on Standard Fibresand at Southwell, and with no genuine rival for the lead he can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without being pressured into burning out early. Liosa and Belsito are the two prominent-style runners who will track close to the pace, meaning the early order is likely to be orderly rather than contested, producing a rhythmic tempo that suits horses able to travel close to the action. The field is overloaded with hold-up types — Fifty Nifty, D Flawless, Beyond Borders, Not Me, Modern Times, Cairdeas and Pickersgill are all genuine closers who cannot all secure their natural position and will be shuffled wide or into tighter berths than ideal, reducing the finishing power of the back half of the field. With a lone front-runner setting a sustainable pace and true hold-up horses unlikely to generate sufficient ground to close from off a slow early tempo on this flat, left-handed circuit, this race shape clearly favours prominent racers and those who can track within two to three lengths of Monsieur Kodi through the first three furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kodi Controls, Prominent Win
scenarios.trigger: If Monsieur Kodi dictates an uncontested, measured pace and the prominent trackers Liosa and Belsito travel comfortably in his slipstream.
scenarios.body: Monsieur Kodi's controlled gallop means the pace is honest but not punishing, leaving Liosa and Belsito fresh to challenge in the final two furlongs while the hold-up brigade find insufficient room or pace to close the gap.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely steady and Monsieur Kodi's rivals fail to close from off the pace in time.
scenarios.body: A conservative tempo on the flat Southwell track can flatter a front-runner who has dominated the early fractions, and with the hold-up horses facing a congested run the leader simply outstays his challengers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Break Through
scenarios.trigger: If Monsieur Kodi sets a faster-than-expected pace and the field fans wide in the straight, creating a late-run opportunity.
scenarios.body: A quicker tempo would compress finishing positions and allow the best-placed of the redistributed hold-up horses — Bright and Hierarchy, who have genuine Standard-going course form — to charge through a tired field in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is misjudged, the field bunches badly at the two-furlong pole and a lower-rated runner times a late run perfectly.
scenarios.body: Congestion and a muddling gallop can produce a fluke sectional for a horse drawn or positioned to exploit a gap, with Pickersgill or Cairdeas benefiting from having the right draw and a late burst.

watchPoints.text: Liosa ran just two days ago — monitor market moves and any jockey report; if the quick turnaround has left any residual fatigue, Belsito becomes the primary prominent-tracker to benefit.

Monsieur Kodi's pace-setting is the structural key to this race — if Oisin Orr goes too conservatively the hold-up horses gain nothing and prominent runners dominate; if he goes too fast he invites closers, so watch the opening two furlongs carefully.

The hold-up contingent is so large that D Flawless, Beyond Borders and Fifty Nifty — all genuine closers — are likely to be forced wide or into bumping ground in the straight; any horse drawn towards the inner with a clear passage benefits disproportionately.

Cairdeas and D Flawless share trainer Paul Midgley — watch for stable intentions, as one may be ridden to set up the other, which could alter how the hold-up group shapes up in the final two furlongs.

Bright is the only hold-up horse with a recent Southwell Standard win (1/6f/STA) and strong similar-going stats (9/15 runs placed or better); if the pace quickens in the middle third this is the late closer with the best profile to capitalise.
